trial_court: Principal Judge, Family Court, Sasaram, Rohtas (Matrimonial Suit No.25/05 and Matrimonial Suit No..36/05)
case_name: Anil Kumar vs Smt. Rakhi Gupta & Anr.

parties.respondent_defendant: Smt. Rakhhi Gupta and Sri Amirchand Prasad Gupta, wife and her father-in-law

facts_of_case: The husband filed a suit for restitution of conjugal rights and the wife filed a suit for divorce on grounds of cruelty. The parties could not amicably resolve issues including custody of their minor son, permanent alimony, and return of the wife's ornaments and clothes.

legal_principles.principle: A lady who was married in a family having several house properties, a car and a motorcycle cannot be asked to lead a wretched life at a monthly allowance of Rs.1000/-.
legal_principles.held: Considering status and property of the appellant, in our view, the grant of monthly maintenance by way of permanent alimony to the wife at the rate of Rs.2500/- per month is not at all excessive.

legal_principles.principle: The jurisdiction of the Family Court is wide enough to entertain a claim by the wife for her ornaments and clothes even in a proceeding under the Hindu Marriage Act.
legal_principles.held: Section 7 of the Family Courts Act and a judgment of the Bombay High Court in the case of Sangeeta B. Kadam v. Balkrishna Ramchandra Kadam, AIR 2005 Bombay 262
cited_cases: Sangeeta B. Kadam v. Balkrishna Ramchandra Kadam, AIR 2005 Bombay 262

outcome.final_order: The trial court's decree for divorce was upheld, along with an order for permanent alimony at Rs.2500/- per month for the husband and wife, and a decree in favour of the respondent wife for a sum of Rs.one lakh in lieu of value of her ornaments and clothes.
